title: An ethanol-based method for quantitative recovery of branchiobdellidans from the crayfish Cambaroides japonicus (De Haan, 1841) (Decapoda: Astacidea: Cambaroididae), with an evaluation of host survival
content:
Abstract
Accurately quantifying symbiont abundance per host individual is essential for understanding host-symbiont interactions. Crayfish are known to harbor branchiobdellidans on their body surfaces and within their gill chambers, yet quantitative studies of these symbiotic worms remain limited because existing collection methods are typically lethal to the host. We developed a simple, field-applicable isolation method for branchiobdellidans from the Japanese crayfish Cambaroides japonicus (De Haan, 1841). Individual crayfish were sequentially immersed and shaken for 30 seconds each in 70% ethanol in stream water. This procedure recovered, on average, 93.4% of branchiobdellidans from host individuals. Laboratory survival experiments showed no mortality and no significant effects on feeding or growth rate, although a transient reduction in weight gain was observed during the first two weeks after treatment. These results demonstrate that the ethanol-water shaking method provides a simple, quantitative, and non-lethal approach for sampling branchiobdellidans from live crayfish. The method is readily applicable under field conditions, including for threatened species, and facilitates ecological studies of crayfish-symbiont interactions without compromising host populations.
